name: .files workflow
content: Treat GitHub issues/projects as the work source of truth and preserve unrelated changes. Use focused conventional feature/fix branch names such as feat/<topic> or fix/<topic>; never use agent/* as a branch prefix. Keep one Nix app module per app: Open WebUI server configuration belongs in modules/server-apps/open-webui/default.nix rather than being split into open-webui-*.nix modules. Prefer small readable diffs. Run checks before completion; check reports problems and does not silently mutate unrelated files. Do not merge a PR unless the user explicitly asks to merge it.

name: Infrastructure documentation
content: Read the relevant infrastructure-docs pages before infrastructure changes. NETWORKING.md is canonical for IP addresses, ports, DNS names, access paths, and network policy; update it first when those change, and have other docs link rather than duplicate its tables. Direct edits, commits, and pushes to infrastructure-docs are allowed. After a documentation change, ensure the commit exists remotely and update the .files infrastructure-docs submodule pointer on the active feature branch. Never point the submodule at an unpushed commit.

name: NixOS server maintenance
content: Operate nixos-server as an always-on trusted worker. Inspect current state before mutation, use the configured localhost-only Open WebUI host-admin path for privileged commands, and do not require the Mac to be online. For NixOS changes: inspect the diff, evaluate/build before switching where practical, perform the switch, then verify the affected units, ports, logs, and persisted state. If a rebuild or service restart interrupts the agent, inspect current system/Git state first and continue only unfinished work rather than blindly replaying side effects.

name: Git and pull-request workflow
description: Branch, commit, PR, and review conventions.
content: Before changing an existing issue/PR, fetch its current state. Work on a focused non-agent-prefixed branch, keep commits intentional, and keep the PR body aligned with actual implementation and validation. If the user requests merge-ready work, implement, validate, run an independent review, feed findings back into the branch, fix them, and re-review until no actionable blockers remain. Leave the PR open and unmerged unless merging was explicitly requested.

name: Agent Mail Rust coordination
description: Coordinate parallel coding agents through the Pi-hosted Agent Mail Rust mailbox.
content: Use the shared Agent Mail Rust MCP service on nixos-server when more than one agent may work on the same repository or live resource. Reuse the existing project/mailbox instead of creating a duplicate; for .files coordination use the canonical project key /home/joshan/.files. Register an agent identity before parallel work, use focused repository-relative file reservations for overlapping paths, communicate through specific threads, read and acknowledge relevant inbox messages, and release reservations promptly when finished. Before any live mutation or deployment test on nixos-server, acquire the established Agent Mail resource/lease nixos-server-live; if it is occupied, continue non-live work and retry later rather than colliding. Release nixos-server-live immediately after live testing. Reservations are advisory coordination, not permission to overwrite another agent. Do not use broadcast-style messaging. GitHub/issues remain the task source of truth.

name: Testing and validation
content: Choose checks that exercise the real failure modes of the change. For Nix, evaluate the affected NixOS configuration and run repository quality checks. For services, verify startup ordering, health endpoints, listening addresses, permissions, persistence, restart behavior, and logs. For integrations, verify both sides of the protocol with the exact pinned versions. Report skipped runtime checks explicitly; do not replace a missing integration test with a claim based only on static inspection.

name: Deployment workflow
description: Safe autonomous deployment and post-deploy verification.
content: Treat deployment as part of the implementation, not as an assumption. Confirm the intended host/branch, acquire the Agent Mail Rust nixos-server-live resource before mutating or testing the live NixOS server when another agent may be active, build/evaluate first where possible, deploy, then verify health and expected behavior. Preserve rollback information. Do not stop after a successful command exit if the service can still be unhealthy. Release nixos-server-live promptly after live mutation/testing.

name: Shopping research
description: Verify exact variants and delivered AUD cost.
content: For shopping comparisons, search broadly first, then open direct product pages for finalists. Verify the exact required variant/specification, current stock, destination Australia, item price, shipping, GST/tax, and delivered total in AUD. Reject teaser prices belonging to unrelated variants and reject dead/404 URLs. Use a real Chromium session when price, stock, locale, login, or variant selection is dynamic; keep authenticated/personal browser state separate from disposable research browsing where practical.

name: Agent session continuity
description: Preserve native agent identity while Open WebUI remains canonical.
content: Open WebUI is the canonical visible conversation workspace. On each participating machine, keep SessionWiki local and expose its read-only stdio MCP through that machine's Computer for search, inspection, tracing, and briefing. Native continuation does not depend on sidebar mirroring: use the SessionWiki ID and Computer run_command on the source host to run `sessionwiki resume <id> --print --no-sync`, then execute the returned native resume command in an already-registered trusted workspace. The optional `open-webui-native-session-mirror` may push SessionWiki transcripts over the existing SSH path to nixos-server so externally-started sessions appear as read-through Open WebUI history entries. Those mirrors are convenience views, not a bidirectional session database or the native agent runtime; native session files remain the resume source. Removing or never running the mirror must not affect SessionWiki discovery or native resume. Do not run a custom session bridge daemon, proxy SessionWiki over another port, write directly into Computer or Open WebUI chat databases, infer unsupported session IDs, or trust a session-reported working directory as a launch path.
